newsitem.title: KENYA: 64 arrested for weapons offences in Kenya election.
newsitem.headline: 64 arrested for weapons offences in Kenya election.

text.p: Police arrested 64 people for possession of offensive weapons including clubs, swords and petrol bombs during a parliamentary by-election near Kenya's capital on Tuesday, Kenyan commercial KTN television said.
It said the weapons were found in two vehicles, one of which was owned by an activist of the ruling Kenya African National Union (KANU) party.
The 64 would appear in court on Tuesday, the report said.
A police officer displayed the weapons, including a petrol bomb with shards of metal inside the bottle and whips.

The seat in Langata, which includes slums, fell vacant when its parliamentarian Raila Odinga left the opposition Ford-Kenya party because of a leadership dispute and joined the little-known National Development Party.
Odinga, who is standing to retain his seat in parliament, won with 40 percent of the vote in Kenya's first multi-party elections in 1992 when the candidate for KANU came third.
The by-election result is due late on Tuesday or on Wednesday.
Analysts widely expect President Daniel arap Moi, 72, and KANU to win Kenya's general election which is due this year.
But social tensions are running high with the government admitting high levels of poverty and Kenya regularly pilloried abroad for its abuse of human rights and rampant official corruption.
